text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $135.72, giving back some of yesterday's sharp 0.8% gain. The decline came despite oil prices holding relatively steady—U.S. crude at $91.48 and global crude at $96.02—suggesting the move was driven more by profit-taking after a three-day rally (the stock jumped from $132.49 to $137.20 between August 31 and September 2) than by fresh negative news in the energy market itself.

The broader oil market remains supported by geopolitical tension: Iran's missile strikes on Kuwait this week have pushed U.S. oil prices up more than 9% for the week, a tailwind for oil producers. However, today's retreat likely reflects normal consolidation after a quick run-up, and possibly some caution as markets assess President Trump's statement that renewed Mideast hostilities won't last "too long"—suggesting possible near-term de-escalation.
